verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report, Sections 5.5 Market overview: cargo and 5.6.2 Cargo volume

candidate_sentences.text: Cargo volume grew by 5.1% to 13.8 million tonnes, with liquid bulk seeing a substantial 47% increase, partly recovering from previous sanction-related declines.

verified_key_information_units.information: Major strategic infrastructure investments including completion of multifunctional quay at Paldiski South Harbour, Muuga Harbour quay reinforcement for large vessels, and ongoing design work for Old City Harbour Terminal A and shore power capacity.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report, Section 5.10 Investments and development prospects

candidate_sentences.text: Capital investments totaled EUR 33.2 million, a 14.4% decrease from the previous year, focusing on infrastructure upgrades at Paldiski South Harbour and Muuga Harbour, as well as ferry maintenance.

verified_key_information_units.information: Dividend distribution of EUR 19.199 million (EUR 0.073 per share) representing 100% of prior year profit, aligned with policy, accompanied by share price appreciation to EUR 1.296 (+22.7%).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report, Sections 5.11 Dividends and 5.12 Share and shareholders

candidate_sentences.text: The company continued its shareholder-friendly policy, distributing a dividend of EUR 19.2 million, which represented 100% of the prior year’s profit.

verified_key_information_units.information: Adverse impact of Russia-Ukraine war reducing liquid bulk volumes and eliminating St. Petersburg cruise calls, partially mitigated by winter cruise season extension, regional marketing, and economic recovery in Estonia and Nordic partners.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report, Sections 5.2 Economic environment and 5.3 Impact of Russia-Ukraine war

verified_key_information_units.information: Icebreaker Botnica operated at reduced utilization rate (49%) with lower charter revenue, but participated in international rescue operations for cargo ship MV Thamesborg in Canadian Arctic waters.

candidate_sentences.text: This minor decrease was primarily driven by a sharp reduction in charter fees from the icebreaker Botnica, which fell by 34% to EUR 7.9 million due to a lower utilization rate of 49%.

verified_key_information_units.information: Environmental sustainability progress including 77% renewable energy usage in operations, GHG emissions reduction of 11% YoY to 19,261 tonnes CO2e, and initiatives for shore power and waste circularity at Old City Harbour.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report, Section 3 Environment and CEO letter (Section 1.4)

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, K4, K5, and K7 are PRESENT with clear coverage in the candidate summary. K6 and K8 are MISSING entirely—no mention of war impacts or environmental sustainability metrics. The summary captures most core financial and operational themes, but the absence of two HIGH/MEDIUM criteria (war impact and sustainability) prevents a perfect score. The overall picture is strong but incomplete.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary demonstrates strong internal logical coherence. All statements build upon each other without contradiction. The summary begins with an overview of financial performance (S1), then systematically details revenue components (S2-S7), operational metrics (S8-S11), cost management and profitability (S12-S16), financial position (S17-S18), capital investments (S19), and dividend policy (S20), concluding with an overall assessment (S21). Explanations for changes (e.g., icebreaker Botnica's reduced utilization impacting revenue, offset by core port growth) are clear and logically connected. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, organizational issues, or unnecessary repetition. The relationships between causes and effects (e.g., cost reductions leading to improved profitability) are consistently supported throughout the text.
